- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast spikes upward, reduce peak predictions by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment drops sharply (≤0.3) after a spike, model should not overcorrect downward — allow a slight lagged rebound.  
- Forecast mean should align with recent 7–14 day average of history, not latest 3–5 days.  
- Overshoots after sentiment peaks (e.g., >85% above recent high) should be capped at +10% of prior peak.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 3–5% to avoid mean reversion miss.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extreme outliers (>±15% from 14-day moving average) unless sentiment confirms strong directional bias.
